takeaways: Sales beat, earnings matched: net sales of $2.56 billion, up 16.7%, vs $2.49 billion expected, and adjusted EPS of $0.30 in line with the $0.30 consensus (Investing.com). GAAP diluted EPS was $0.29.

International is the growth engine: sales outside the U.S. rose 28.1% to $1.20 billion and are now 47% of total net sales. LATAM jumped 48.8% in dollars, led by Brazil, per CEO Hilton Schlosberg (Investing.com).
Monster Energy Drinks segment sales rose 17.1% to $2.37 billion. Strategic Brands grew 19.8% to $156.4 million. Alcohol Brands fell 13.6% to $28.5 million.
The company bought back about 2.3 million shares for roughly $100 million in the quarter, with about $800 million still authorized as of the prior Monday (Investing.com).
Investing.com reported shares down roughly 5% after hours despite the revenue beat; Yahoo Finance showed about $45.08 vs a $47.83 regular-session close.
verdict: Monster sold a lot of cans, matched the EPS number on the nose, and still got a 5% after-hours slap. That's the market saying 'cool growth, where's the margin party?' International is ripping, alcohol is shrinking, and caffeine alone couldn't keep the stock awake past 4 p.m.

sources.title: Investing.com: Monster Beverage shares fall despite Q3 revenue beat
